lead.text: JWE decompression bomb (zip bomb): jose/jwe.py:453 calls zlib.decompress(compressed) with NO max_length argument and no post-decompression size check. The attacker fully controls both the trigger and the payload via the JWE token passed to the jwe.decrypt() entry point: _jwe_compact_deserialize(jwe_str) (jwe.py:79) parses the raw token, header is json.loads()'d from the base64url header segment (jwe.py:276->300), and decrypt() then calls _decompress(header.get("zip"), plain_text) at jwe.py:187. The only guards in _decompress are name checks on the zip algorithm -- 'zip not in ZIPS.SUPPORTED' (line 448), 'zip is None' (450), 'zip == ZIPS.DEF' (452) -- none of which bound the output size. An attacker sets the protected header to {"alg":"RSA-OAEP","enc":"A256GCM","zip":"DEF"} and supplies a few KB of highly-compressible deflate data that expands to multiple GB, exhausting memory/CPU in the decrypting process. Because RSA-OAEP / RSA1_5 / ECDH-ES are PUBLIC-key encryption, any unauthenticated party holding the recipient's public key can mint a valid token, so this needs no shared secret. Fix: pass a bounded max_length to zlib.decompress (or use a decompressobj with an output cap) and reject oversized output.

lead.text: AES-CBC-HMAC padding oracle -- ciphertext is decrypted and PKCS7-unpadded BEFORE the MAC is verified. In jose/jwe.py:_decrypt_and_auth (method at line 208), line 239 runs 'plaintext = encryption_key.decrypt(cipher_text, iv, aad, auth_tag)' and only AFTERWARDS does line 240 check 'auth_tag != auth_tag_check' -> raise JWEError("Invalid JWE Auth Tag") (line 241). For the A*CBC-HS* encs (selected by 'enc in ALGORITHMS.HMAC_AUTH_TAG', line 230), the backend performs NO authentication at all: jose/backends/cryptography_backend.py CryptographyAESKey.decrypt (method line 490) takes the non-GCM branch at line 505 and runs Cipher(algorithms.AES(...), mode).decryptor() -> decryptor.update(cipher_text) (507) -> decryptor.finalize() (508) -> PKCS7(...).unpadder() (509) -> unpadder.update(padded_plain_text) (510) -> unpadder.finalize() (511). unpadder.finalize() raises on invalid PKCS7 padding, producing an error distinguishable from the later 'Invalid JWE Auth Tag' -- a classic padding oracle. cipher_text, iv and auth_tag are all attacker-controlled, split straight out of the token at jwe.py:273 and base64url-decoded. lead.text: Attacker-controlled UNVERIFIED 'alg' header selects the at_hash digest algorithm and can raise an unhandled KeyError. jose/jwt.py:146 reads the algorithm straight out of the unauthenticated token header -- 'algorithm = jws.get_unverified_header(token)["alg"]' -- and passes it to _validate_claims(..., algorithm=algorithm, ...) at jwt.py:156, where it is used as a raw dict index at jwt.py:448: 'calculate_at_hash(access_token, ALGORITHMS.HASHES[algorithm])'.
